title: A REQUEST THAT LOOKED LIKE RETREAT

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: They said, "If we have found favor in your eyes, let this land be given to your servants as our possession. Do not make us cross the Jordan." When Moses heard this, he was troubled, and he asked the Reubenites and Gadites, "Should your fellow Israelites go to war while you sit here?" - Num 32:5-6 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The request came out plainly: "Do not make us cross the Jordan." They wanted to settle on this side and let the rest of the nation go on to fight for the Promised Land without them. To Moses, this sounded painfully familiar — it echoed the fear of the previous generation who had refused to enter the land at all. His response was sharp and searching: "Should your brothers go to war while you sit here?"

Moses was not against them prospering. He was troubled by the possibility that their comfort would come at the cost of the whole community's mission. It is a heart-check question for all of us: am I willing to let others carry the burden while I settle into ease? God never intended His people to be a collection of individuals each grabbing their own comfort. We belong to one another.

There is a subtle danger in Christian life of quietly stepping back — letting others do the serving, the giving, the praying, the going — while we enjoy the benefits. The New Testament calls us to carry one another's burdens (Gal 6:2) and to consider others' interests, not only our own (Phil 2:4).

Jesus is the great example. He did not sit in the comfort of heaven while we struggled; He entered the battle for us, laying down His life. Following Him means we do not settle into ease while our brothers and sisters still fight. We go together.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Are there ways you have quietly stepped back and let others carry the load?
2. How does belonging to God's family shape your view of comfort?
3. Where is God calling you to stand alongside others rather than settle apart?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, forgive me when I choose ease over standing with Your people. Help me to carry burdens with others and to follow Christ, who entered the battle for me. Amen.
